content.text: I have surveyed the pricing, fee-tier, Supplemental Payments, support and termination provisions and searched for parity language.

input.quote: During the term of the non-exclusive license agreement, Licensor shall receive from Licensee one third (33%) of the gross amounts earned by the Licensee from third parties applicable to the following areas of the Licensed Technology usage (if any), ("Supplemental Payments"):
input.rationale: No most-favoured-nation or pricing-parity obligation runs against us. Searches for "favorable/favourable", "most favored", "best", "discount", "any other customer" and "other licensees" return no parity language. The commercial terms (per-US$1m fee tiers at p0058–p0063, Supplemental Payments at p0074–p0083, rebate shares at p0075–p0076, support fees at p0086–p0089) are fixed-consideration and revenue-share provisions, not obligations to extend to the Licensor terms no less favourable than those we grant third parties: the 33% Supplemental Payment is a flat revenue share on defined categories, with no benchmarking to third-party terms. The only "other licensees" reference (p0094) runs in our favour — Licensor must make Revisions available to us when it makes them generally available to its other licensees. Separately, Article XXII's Right of First Refusal (p0139–p0141) and the Change of Control consent (p0134) do burden us on an exit, but they are M&A/assignment controls rather than commercial best-terms parity, so they fall outside this rule and should be addressed under the change-of-control/assignment playbook rules. No redline proposed under the MFN rule.
